Chapter 14. The Cross and the Promise of Home
You know, deep down, we all crave a place where we truly belong—a home where we’re seen, accepted, and loved just as we are. As we wrap up this journey, let’s come back to that longing.
Picture this: someone spends years searching, wandering from place to place, never quite feeling at home. Then, one day, they finally find a community where the welcome is genuine. Or maybe it’s someone who always felt like an outsider, only to discover they have a seat at the table, just waiting for them.
That’s the kind of home the cross creates—a place where shame melts away and acceptance takes its place, where old wounds are met with real compassion.
Most of us carry around this quiet ache, a sense of exile, like we don’t quite fit in anywhere. And here’s the beautiful thing: the cross speaks right to that feeling. It promises we’re never truly alone. It’s more than an invitation to a physical place—it’s a call to relationship, to come home to belonging.
The stories shared here make it real. There’s a teenager, worn out by years of rejection, who suddenly finds themselves embraced by a group of friends. Or an elder, carrying a lifetime of regret, who’s welcomed with open arms.
Home, when it’s shaped by the cross, isn’t perfect. But it’s real. It’s built on grace—grace that says you don’t have to earn your spot. Love is the natural language here, spoken in small acts of kindness every day.
The cross assures us of one thing: no matter how far you’ve wandered, there’s always a way back. There’s always a place for you.
